newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sentences two HK men to death for drugs.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sentences two HK men to death for drugs.

text.p: Two Hong Kong residents were sentenced to death by a court in Vietnam on Friday for illegal trafficking in drugs, a court official said.
Both holders of British passports, the two were arrested at Ho Chi Minh City airport in March 1996 after 18.1 kg (40 lb) of heroin was found concealed in false-bottomed cases.
British diplomats said Sun Chi Kin and Chan Chun Hung Sammy had 15 days to appeal against their sentence before going before a firing squad.
Sun and Chan had been travelling with fake Portuguese passports and under false names when they were arrested.
Diplomats said the authorities had granted consular access to the men for the first time last December.

A consulate official who attended part of the one-day trial on Friday said she had spoken to them briefly before the hearing got under way, but was stopped by officials from continuing the conversation.
A Hong Kong man was found guilty of a similar crime and executed in 1995.
A Vietnamese-Canadian woman was sentenced to death last week in Hanoi after being found guilty of attempting to smuggle 5.45 kg (12 pounds) of heroin out of the country.
Canadian diplomats said they had not yet been able to ascertain through the courts if the 41-year-old woman had appealed.

Drugs experts say Vietnam is both a growing market and a transit route for narcotics from the notorious Golden Triangle opium-poppy growing area, which straddles the borders of Laos, Burma and Thailand. Heroin is derived from opium.
A senior local judge, Nguyen Du Sau, told Reuters ahead of Friday's trial that the amount of heroin found in the two Hong Kong mens' possession was the biggest haul yet in Vietnam.
